title: Deferred Compensation in Multiperiod Labor Contracts: An Experimental Test of Lazear's Model

original_source.version_note: Pre-publication author manuscript matching title/authors and central contribution; exact final wording may differ.

central_claims: Experimental multiperiod labor contracts test whether credible deferred compensation elicits sufficient worker effort to avoid dismissal, and compare commitment, reciprocity, and reputation.

source_manifest.title: Deferred Compensation in Multiperiod Labor Contracts: An Experimental Test of Lazear's Model
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether enforced commitment raises deferred worker earnings w2+w3; replication N=160, original focal N=120, p=.142. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

answers.rationale: No unambiguous later independent support for the stated central claim was established in the sources read.
The available evidence does not settle successful independent reproduction of the central claim.

The selected deferred-pay prediction (w2+w3) did not survive the larger independent preregistered comparison: N=160 versus 120, p=.142. This does not reject every Lazear-model or worker-effort claim in the paper.
